Goal: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Required evaluation protocol: Shared evaluation protocol (from limitation group C: G2, G10, G12, G16): checkpoints and hyper-parameters are selected on a held-out validation split of the SOURCE modalities and never on the target test set, and the MVFA baseline is re-run under the same rule; results are reported under a modality-disjoint leave-one-modality-out split (RESC and OCT17 are held out together, never one with the other in training), with patient-level separation where identifiers exist, over at least 3 random seeds and 3 few-shot support draws with mean and standard deviation, and against the missing baselines named in G12 where relevant.
Parent hypotheses: Parent 1:
TITLE: DINOv2-affinity propagation of label-restricted pseudo-masks for mask-free MVFA training
SUMMARY: Grow confident CLIP pseudo-mask seeds over a DINOv2 patch-affinity graph with a random walk, and train MVFA's segmentation adapters on the propagated masks.
HYPOTHESIS: DINOv2-affinity propagation with T = 3 increases pseudo-mask Dice by at least 10 points over seed-only pseudo-masks, and MVFA trained on the propagated masks attains at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: target type: true masks; seed-only pseudo-masks (problem rule); DINOv2-affinity propagated pseudo-masks with walk length T in {1, 3, 5}. Affinity A_ij = exp(cos(g_i, g_j)/tau) over the 8-neighbourhood and top-10 feature neighbours of DINOv2 ViT-B/14 patch features g at 224 px (16x16 grid), row-normalised; propagated score s_T = A^T s_0 with s_0 the binary seed map; final mask = s_T > 0.5 x max(s_T) intersected with the image being labelled abnormal. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask Dice vs true masks; pixel AUROC and Dice of the trained model on held-out masked modalities.
RATIONALE: Label-restricted pseudo-masks from CLIP features are fragmented: only the most atypical patches pass the 99th-percentile threshold, so lesions appear as scattered seeds. Spatial-FAD shows that DINO's patch affinities capture anatomical structure and lesion boundaries better than CLIP. Propagating the confident seeds over a DINOv2 affinity graph turns fragments into coherent regions while staying inside the abnormal image, which should give the segmentation adapters better targets.
METHOD: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute seed maps with the problem rule (CLIP level-4, 99th percentile on source validation). 2) Load DINOv2 ViT-B/14 via torch.hub ('facebookresearch/dinov2', 'dinov2_vitb14'); extract normalised patch tokens at 224 px. 3) Resample seeds to the 16x16 DINO grid; build sparse A (8-neighbours + 10 feature NNs, tau = 0.1). 4) s_T = A^T s_0, T = 3 (selected on source validation where masks exist in the source fold); threshold at 0.5 max; upsample to 240 px. 5) dataset/medical_zero.py loads the propagated masks; train_zero.py unchanged (Focal + Dice). 6) Runtime: one forward pass of DINOv2 per abnormal image, minutes on one GPU. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; seed-only; propagated with T in {1,3,5}; masks removed from 1 and 3 sources. Ablation: CLIP-feature affinity instead of DINOv2 affinity (isolates the structural prior). Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice/IoU, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if DINOv2 propagation does not beat CLIP-affinity propagation and seed-only masks on pseudo-mask Dice.

Parent 2:
TITLE: Mixing label-restricted pseudo-masks with exact synthetic-lesion masks for mask-free MVFA localisation
SUMMARY: Train MVFA's segmentation adapters on real abnormal images with pseudo-masks plus normal images carrying synthetic lesions with exact masks, and find the mixing ratio that best recovers mask-supervised localisation.
HYPOTHESIS: A mixture with rho between 0.25 and 0.5 recovers at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities and beats both pure pseudo-masks (rho = 0) and pure synthesis (rho = 1) by at least 2 pixel-AUROC points.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: fraction rho of segmentation-branch training samples that are synthetic (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0), with the rest being real abnormal images with label-restricted pseudo-masks (problem rule). Synthetic lesions are created per source dataset from its own images: a random elliptical region (area 0.5-8% of the image) of a normal image is replaced by a Poisson-blended patch cut from an abnormal image's pseudo-anomalous area (so texture is realistic), or by an intensity-perturbed blob (Gaussian intensity shift of +-0.3 x local std) when no anomalous patch exists; the mask is the pasted region. Dependent variables: pixel AUROC and Dice on held-out masked modalities, image AUROC, and the false-positive rate on normal test images at the source-selected threshold.
RATIONALE: Pseudo-masks on real abnormal images have realistic appearance but noisy extents; synthetic lesions pasted into normal images of the same dataset have exact extents but unrealistic appearance. Fed-LoRA shows synthetic abnormal images help few-shot anomaly detection when tailored to the domain. Training the segmentation adapters on a mixture of the two sources should combine their strengths, and the mixing ratio is the key variable.
METHOD: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute label-restricted pseudo-masks for real abnormal source images (problem rule). 2) synth.py: function synth_lesion(normal_img, donor_img, donor_mask) using cv2.seamlessClone (Poisson) with an elliptical mask; fallback blob perturbation. 3) dataset/medical_zero.py: a MixedSegDataset that, per iteration, draws a synthetic sample with probability rho, else a real abnormal sample with pseudo-mask (normal images also drawn as in MVFA). 4) train_zero.py: unchanged losses (Focal + Dice on seg branch, BCE on det branch); synthetic images labelled abnormal for the det branch. 5) Select rho and checkpoint on source-validation pixel AUROC against pseudo-masks (no target data). Hyper-parameters as MVFA (lr 1e-3, 50 epochs, 240 px).
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: rho in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}; reference with true masks. Ablation: Poisson-blended real texture vs intensity blobs only. Metrics: pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC, normal-image FPR. Falsified if no intermediate rho beats both extremes by 2 points or if the best mixture recovers less than 80% of the mask-supervised gain.
